Optimal.Notes: The 40 fps / 40 Hz lock is the sweet spot for this game on Deck — it holds during campaign map play and most battles, dropping only in the heaviest multi-army clashes. FSR from 1024x640 produces an acceptable image at native 800p for a strategy title viewed mostly from a distance.

profiles.Summary: Total War: WARHAMMER III is a demanding grand strategy/real-time tactics title that pushes the Steam Deck hard, particularly during large battles with many units; expect 30–45 fps depending on settings and battle scale. It carries a ProtonDB gold rating with no Deck-specific reports found, so profiles are estimated from PC requirements and hardware comparisons.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck or ProtonDB detail reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs, the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU class (~GTX 1050 Ti), and the game's known CPU/GPU demands. On your first run, check frame rate during a mid-size battle and fall back to the Max Battery profile if it cannot hold 30 fps.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to 800p keeps GPU load low enough for the 8 W TDP limit; large battles may still dip below 30 fps briefly. Locking to 30 fps with a 40 Hz refresh rate eliminates tearing and smooths out frame pacing.

The game requires 120 GB of storage, which may strain smaller Deck SSDs or microSD cards.
Large late-game battles with many units and spell effects can cause significant frame-rate drops even on capable PCs.
No native Linux build; runs via Proton — occasional shader compilation stutters on first launch are likely.

MaxPerformance.Notes: 60 fps is achievable on the campaign map and smaller skirmishes, but large end-game battles will drop to the mid-30s — consider dropping Unit Detail to Low before major battles to recover headroom. Battery life is short at 15 W TDP, so keep a charger handy for extended sessions.

Optimal.Notes: Medium textures and unit detail look noticeably better on the OLED screen while still targeting a stable 30 fps cap; FSR at 1024x640 keeps the image sharp enough for the strategy view. Expect dips into the high 20s during the largest battles — the 30 fps cap smooths out the overall feel.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 and upscaling with FSR gives the GPU the most headroom; large battles will still dip, so consider pausing in the most intense moments. TDP cap at 8 W and a fixed GPU clock keep heat and battery draw in check on the campaign map.

Full 15 W TDP and auto GPU clock let the APU boost freely; expect the battery to drain quickly and the unit to run warm during extended battle sequences.
